options: at a corner point of the feasible region

options: every point of the segment from (4, 4) to (6, 0)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT part of an LPP?

sections.title: Objective type questions of two 1-mark parts.

questions.q: (a) The common region satisfying all constraints is the ______ region. (b) Z = 2x + 3y at corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 3) and (3, 2) is maximum at ______.
A firm makes chairs (x) and tables (y). Each chair needs 2 hours and each table 3 hours; 30 hours are available. Profit is ₹40 per chair and ₹70 per table. Formulate the LPP.
questions.answer:
Maximise Z = 40x + 70y
subject to 2x + 3y ≤ 30, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.

questions.q: A dealer has ₹5760 to buy fans (₹360 each) and sewing machines (₹240 each), and space for at most 20 items. Profit is ₹22 per fan and ₹18 per machine. Formulate the LPP and find the maximum profit.
questions.answer:
Maximise Z = 22x + 18y subject to 360x + 240y ≤ 5760 (3x + 2y ≤ 48), x + y ≤ 20, x, y ≥ 0.
Corners: (0, 0), (16, 0), (8, 12), (0, 20).
Z: 0, 352, 176 + 216 = 392, 360.
Maximum profit ₹392 with 8 fans and 12 sewing machines.

questions.q: Find the maximum and minimum of Z = x + 2y subject to x + 2y ≥ 100, 2x − y ≤ 0, 2x + y ≤ 200, x, y ≥ 0, graphically.
questions.answer:
Corners of the feasible region: x + 2y = 100 meets x = 0 at (0, 50) and 2x − y = 0 at (20, 40); 2x − y = 0 meets 2x + y = 200 at (50, 100); 2x + y = 200 meets x = 0 at (0, 200).
Z(0, 50) = 100, Z(20, 40) = 100, Z(50, 100) = 250, Z(0, 200) = 400.
Maximum 400 at (0, 200); minimum 100 at every point of the segment joining (0, 50) and (20, 40).

or.q: A drink needs at least 80 units of chemical A and 60 units of chemical B. Supplier S's packet has 4 units of A and 2 of B and costs ₹10; supplier T's has 1 of A and 1 of B and costs ₹4. Formulate the LPP and find the minimum cost.
or.answer:
Let x packets from S and y from T. Minimise C = 10x + 4y
subject to 4x + y ≥ 80, 2x + y ≥ 60, x, y ≥ 0.
Corners of the (unbounded) region: (0, 80), (10, 40), (30, 0).
C = 320, 260, 300 ⇒ minimum ₹260 at x = 10, y = 40.

questions.q: Minimise and maximise Z = 5x + 2y subject to x − 2y ≤ 2, 3x + 2y ≤ 12, −3x + 2y ≤ 3, x, y ≥ 0.

A machine makes products A and B. A needs 2 units of chemical and 1 of compound; B needs 1 of chemical and 2 of compound. 800 units of chemical and 1000 of compound are available. Profit is ₹30 on A and ₹20 on B. Find the maximum profit.

or.q: Nuts take 1 h on machine A and 3 h on B; bolts take 3 h on A and 1 h on B. Each machine runs at most 12 h a day. Profit ₹17.50 per package of nuts and ₹7 per package of bolts. Maximise profit.
or.answer:
Maximise Z = 17.5x + 7y subject to x + 3y ≤ 12, 3x + y ≤ 12, x, y ≥ 0.
Corners: (0, 0), (4, 0), (3, 3), (0, 4).
Z: 0, 70, 52.5 + 21 = 73.5, 28.
Maximum ₹73.50 with 3 packages of each.

questions.q: Maximise Z = 3x + 4y subject to 2x + y ≤ 1000, x + y ≤ 800, x ≤ 400, y ≤ 700, x, y ≥ 0.

or.q: Fertiliser A has 12% nitrogen and 5% phosphoric acid; B has 4% and 5%. At least 12 kg of each is needed. A costs ₹110/kg and B ₹48/kg. Find the minimum cost.

questions.q: A cooperative has 50 hectares for crops A and B, with profits ₹10,500 and ₹9,000 per hectare. Herbicide use is 20 L/ha for A and 10 L/ha for B, at most 800 L. Maximise profit.

or.q: Minimise Z = 20x + 10y subject to x + 2y ≤ 40, 3x + y ≥ 30, 4x + 3y ≥ 60, x, y ≥ 0.
